results.question: What evidence supports using this Testnet prototype with real money?

lead.text: ResearchAgent is a Testnet prototype, with no mainnet readiness claim.

results.conclusion: ResearchAgent is a Testnet prototype, with no mainnet readiness claim. Testnet transactions can demonstrate that a particular payment mechanism settled on that network; they do not establish suitability for handling real customer funds. A successful receipt is evidence about a specific run. It does not certify legal compliance, commercial reliability, investment quality or regulatory approval. The distinction matters when a judge asks what the demonstrated system is ready to do. For research purchases, the operator wallet pays the writer directly. The application does not receive the writer's payment as an intermediary in that flow. The operator nevertheless controls the payer signing key and the signed payment journal. Describing that limited flow accurately avoids a broader custody claim. The separate hire-the-agent flow receives caller funds before purchases, royalties and change payouts. During that interval the operator wallet holds funds belonging in the flow; the compliance record calls this receive-and-forward custody, rather than a segregated escrow account. The implemented controls provide useful boundaries without constituting a compliance program. Deterministic policy authorizes purchases inside spending caps. Operator pause prevents new spending while submitted work still reconciles. Per-agent authority is subordinate to operator limits. Refunds do not restore gross spending authorization. A hash-chained audit trail records admission, policy, reservation, signature, settlement, delivery and recovery events. Those controls make financial behavior inspectable, but an audit export is not a substitute for licensing, safeguarding, customer identification or an operating procedure. Payee screening currently means an operator-managed exact-address denylist. It is not sanctions screening. A malformed or unreadable denylist fails closed, while a missing list supplies no screening entries. An address match can prevent an unsigned purchase and record a refusal. It cannot identify the person behind a new address, monitor aggregate customer behavior or detect structuring. The compliance record explicitly describes KYC, AML and Travel Rule implementation as absent. These omissions remain omissions even when all five application hard gates pass. Writer Credentials address identity under an operator-trusted issuer. The issuer must establish identity through its own process; the engine does not perform KYC. Credential acceptance, expiration and trusted issuer checks can support an identity attestation. They do not prove that an article is accurate, that its author is independent, or that a payment service is licensed. Our team writer remains unverified and visibly team-authored. Its content receives ordinary trust treatment, with no reputation advantage granted merely because the builders wrote it. The security record also separates development custody from the protections needed for production operations. Private signing material must stay outside model prompts, receipts and public logs. Durable signed obligations need reconciliation after timeouts rather than replacement purchases. A future deployment would need reviewed key custody, rotation, access controls, monitoring and incident response appropriate to its risks. A plan to use a stronger signer is a plan until implemented and verified. Neither this article nor a successful Testnet payment establishes that future work as completed. The practical reading of the evidence is therefore bounded. Check a receipt's exact delivered passages, grants and validated settlement when assessing the demonstrated mechanism. Keep simulated providers and fixture answers labelled. Treat Testnet funds as having no real value. Keep receive-and-forward custody distinct from direct purchases, and identity distinct from article truth. The note records documented limits so a reader can assess readiness honestly; it makes no recommendation to turn on mainnet spending. The source record is docs/COMPLIANCE.md, especially its controls, custody, screening and mainnet sections, together with docs/contracts/SECURITY.md and docs/writer-verification.md. These are implementation descriptions, not a legal opinion.
